display.censoring_note: Only resolved loans enter the sample, so early defaults and early prepayments are over-represented relative to loans that are still open. The censored 2017-2018 window has a higher observed default rate (21.29%) than the mature 2014-2015 window (14.46%), and its loan composition differs, so its AUC is not comparable. The +0.0580 AUC gap is a measurement artifact of the sampling; the censored window is shown only to quantify it and feeds no headline number.
display.calibration_caption: Reliability by predicted-PD decile. Every point lies above the diagonal: observed default exceeds predicted, so the score under-predicts. On the test window the calibrated score is 2.3 pp below the observed rate.
display.calibration_note: Recalibration barely changes the Brier score (raw 0.11949 vs calibrated 0.11970); calibration-in-the-large moves from 0.1844 to 0.1986. The selected method is isotonic, and no method beats the raw score. Every decile lies above the diagonal, so the score under-predicts default: on the test window the calibrated score is 2.3 pp below the observed rate.
display.segments_note: Silhouette 0.1840, stability ARI 0.9566. k-means separates the default rate by only 0.54 pp; a Gaussian mixture separates more (6.28 pp) and is at least as stable (bootstrap ARI 0.9785 vs 0.9566). Neither is used as a model feature.
display.forecast_caption: 17-month holdout: an honest seasonal model is beaten by the naive benchmark
display.forecast_note: A last-value naive forecast wins outright (MASE 0.5543 vs 1.1319 for SARIMAX and 0.5903 for ETS) on the 17-month holdout. Residual autocorrelation is only marginal (Ljung-Box at lag 10, p = 0.066), consistent with a series that is close to a random walk. This is reported as a limitation, not dressed up.

limitations: Discrimination is moderate (champion Gini 0.3144); the lender's own grade still adds about 0.0227 AUC.
Loan-level LGD is not usable (every model has a negative out-of-time R-squared).
Probability calibration is a null result: isotonic did not improve the test Brier (0.11949 raw vs 0.11970 calibrated).
The monthly default-rate forecast is beaten by a naive benchmark (last-value naive MASE 0.5543 vs SARIMAX 1.1319).
Antithetic variates give a negligible variance reduction (reported, not hidden).
No macroeconomic variables; the data ends in 2018, so only one credit cycle is observed.
Reject inference is exploratory only and feeds no headline number. The data contains approved loans only, so the selection bias cannot be corrected.
